module_title: Integrating Inverter, Battery, and Solar Panels

lessons.title: Step-by-Step System Wiring Diagram for a Small Business
lessons.body: To wire a small business solar system, you need a clear plan. Start by drawing your components: solar panels, charge controller, battery bank, inverter, and AC loads. For a typical shop with a fridge, lights, and phone charging, you might use four 250W panels (1000W total), a 60A MPPT charge controller, four 200Ah deep-cycle batteries (24V system), and a 3kVA pure sine wave inverter. Mount panels facing north (in southern Africa) at a 20-30 degree tilt. Use 4mmÂ² solar cable for panel to controller, and 25mmÂ² for battery to inverter. Connect panels in series-parallel to match controller voltage. Run cables through conduit to protect from sun and rain. Connect charge controller to battery bank first, then panels. Connect inverter to battery with thick cables and a 150A DC breaker. Wire AC output to a distribution board with circuit breakers for each load. Ground the panel frames and inverter case. Label all cables. Test with a multimeter before powering loads. Always use fuses or breakers on every positive line. A common mistake is undersizing cables, causing voltage drop and heat. For a 3kVA inverter, use at least 25mmÂ² cable for a 1-2 meter run. Tighten all connections firmly; loose connections cause fires. If you are unsure, hire a qualified solar technician to inspect your work.

lessons.title: Connecting Inverter to Battery Bank and AC Loads
lessons.body: Connecting your inverter correctly is critical for safety and performance. First, ensure your battery bank is wired for the correct voltageâusually 12V, 24V, or 48V. For a 24V system, connect two 12V batteries in series (positive to negative) to make 24V, then parallel additional pairs for more capacity. Use 25mmÂ² or thicker cables for battery-to-inverter connections. Install a DC circuit breaker (rated for at least 1.5 times your inverter's max current) on the positive cable. For a 3kVA 24V inverter, max current is about 125A, so use a 150A breaker. Connect the negative cable last to avoid sparks. Tighten terminals with a wrenchâloose connections overheat. Now for AC loads: the inverter's AC output goes to a small distribution board. Install a 16A or 20A MCB for each circuit (lights, sockets, fridge). Use 2.5mmÂ² copper cable for AC wiring. Connect the inverter's earth terminal to a ground rod or your building's earth. Never connect the inverter's AC output to the grid unless it's a hybrid inverter designed for that. For off-grid, simply plug your loads into the inverter's AC sockets or wire them to the board. Test with a multimeter: check AC voltage (should be 220-240V) and polarity. If the inverter beeps or shows fault, disconnect and check connections. Always turn off the inverter before working on AC wiring.

lessons.title: Setting Up a Hybrid System with Grid or Generator Backup
lessons.body: A hybrid system lets you use solar first, then battery, then grid or generator as backup. This is ideal for areas with unreliable grid power. You need a hybrid inverter (e.g., 5kVA) that can take DC from solar and batteries, and AC from grid or generator. Connect solar panels to the hybrid inverter's PV input (check max voltage, often 500V). Connect battery bank to the battery terminals. Connect grid or generator to the AC input terminals. The inverter will automatically switch between sources. Set priorities: solar > battery > grid. For a small business, set the inverter to use solar during the day, battery at night, and grid only when battery is low (e.g., below 20%). Use a generator of at least 1.5 times the inverter's continuous power to handle surge. Install a changeover switch if you want manual control, but hybrid inverters have automatic transfer. Program the inverter via its LCD or app: set battery type (e.g., lithium or lead-acid), charging current (e.g., 30A), and grid charging times. Ensure the generator is off when grid is present to avoid backfeed. Ground the system properly. Test by simulating a grid outage: turn off grid breaker, see if inverter switches to battery within 20 milliseconds. If it fails, check settings. Always use surge protection on AC input.

lessons.title: Using Changeover Switches and Breakers Safely
lessons.body: Changeover switches and breakers protect you and your equipment. A changeover switch (manual or automatic) lets you switch between grid, generator, and inverter output. For a small business, install a manual changeover switch rated for your total load (e.g., 63A). Connect grid to one input, generator to another, and inverter output to the third. The output goes to your distribution board. Never connect two sources at onceâthat's why changeover switches have mechanical interlock. For breakers: use DC breakers for solar and battery circuits (rated for DC voltage, e.g., 250V DC). AC breakers (MCBs) for grid and load circuits. Size DC breakers at 1.25 times the expected current. For a 60A charge controller, use an 80A DC breaker. For battery-to-inverter, use a 150A DC breaker for 3kVA. Install breakers in a dry, accessible place. Label each breaker clearly: 'Solar In', 'Battery', 'Inverter Out', 'Grid'. Test breakers monthly by switching off and on. Never bypass a breaker. Use fuses for extra protection on small wires. Always turn off the main breaker before working on wiring. If a breaker trips, find the fault before resetting. Use a multimeter to check for shorts. In Africa, power surges are common, so use surge protection devices (SPDs) on AC input. A 40kA SPD costs about $30 and can save your inverter.

lessons.title: Testing Your System Before Powering Your Equipment
lessons.body: Before you plug in your fridge or computer, test the system step by step. First, check all connections are tight and correct. Use a multimeter to measure battery voltage: a 24V bank should read 25.6V when fully charged. Check solar panel open-circuit voltage: for four 250W panels in series, expect around 150V DC. Connect panels to charge controller and check it starts charging. Next, test the inverter without loads: turn it on, measure AC output voltage (should be 230V Â±5%). Check frequency (50Hz). If the inverter has a display, look for error codes. Now, test with a small load like a 100W bulb. It should light steadily. If it flickers, check connections. Then, test with a larger load like a 500W drill. Monitor battery voltageâit should not drop below 22V for a 24V system. If it does, your battery may be undersized. Test the changeover switch: switch from inverter to grid and back, ensuring no interruption to critical loads. Test breakers: trip each one to confirm it cuts power. Check earth leakage: use a socket tester to ensure correct polarity and earth. Finally, run the system for 24 hours with normal loads, checking for overheating cables or unusual noises. Record voltages and currents. If anything is wrong, fix before connecting sensitive equipment. Always wear safety glasses and gloves.

lessons.title: Labelling and Documenting Your Solar Installation
lessons.body: Good labelling and documentation save time and prevent accidents. Start by labelling every cable at both ends: 'PV+', 'PV-', 'Battery+', 'Battery-', 'AC Out', 'Grid In'. Use durable labels or heat-shrink tubing with printed text. Label breakers and switches clearly: 'Main DC', 'Inverter AC Out', 'Solar Breaker'. Create a system diagram showing all components, cable sizes, breaker ratings, and battery wiring. Note the date of installation and battery water topping schedule (if lead-acid). Keep a logbook: record daily energy production (kWh), battery voltage in the morning, and any faults. Take photos of the wiring before closing panels. For the client, provide a simple user manual: how to turn on/off, what to do if breaker trips, and emergency contacts. In Africa, where technicians may be scarce, clear documentation helps anyone service the system. Use a permanent marker or label maker. Avoid paper labels that fall off. Also, document the settings of your hybrid inverter: battery type, charging current, grid charging times. If you sell the business, this documentation adds value. Store a copy in a plastic sleeve near the system. Update it whenever you change anything. A well-documented system is safer, easier to troubleshoot, and more reliable.

quiz.q: What is the correct order to connect a charge controller?
options: A) Connect panels first, then battery
B) Connect battery first, then panels
C) Connect load first, then battery
D) Connect inverter first, then panels
quiz.explanation: Connecting the battery first allows the controller to sense system voltage and avoid damage.

quiz.q: For a 3kVA 24V inverter, what size DC breaker is recommended for battery connection?
quiz.explanation: Max current is about 125A, so a 150A breaker provides safe margin.

quiz.q: What cable size is typically used for battery-to-inverter connections in a small system?
quiz.explanation: 25mmÂ² handles high current with minimal voltage drop for short runs.

quiz.q: Which terminal should be connected last when wiring batteries to an inverter?
quiz.explanation: Connecting negative last reduces spark risk if tools touch metal.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a changeover switch?
options: B) To switch between power sources safely
D) To convert DC to AC
quiz.explanation: It allows manual or automatic transfer between grid, generator, and inverter.

quiz.q: What should you check first before powering AC loads?
options: B) AC output voltage and polarity
quiz.explanation: Incorrect voltage or polarity can damage equipment.

quiz.q: In a hybrid system, what is the typical priority order?
quiz.explanation: Solar is used first, then battery, then grid as backup.

quiz.q: What size generator is recommended for a 5kVA hybrid inverter?
quiz.explanation: Generator should be at least 1.5 times inverter continuous power to handle surge.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a DC breaker in a solar circuit?
options: A) To convert DC to AC
quiz.explanation: DC breakers interrupt fault currents and protect wiring.

quiz.q: What does a multimeter measure when testing a battery bank?
quiz.explanation: DC voltage indicates state of charge and system health.

quiz.q: What is a common cause of inverter overheating?
quiz.explanation: Loose connections create resistance and heat.

quiz.q: Why should you label cables in a solar installation?
options: B) To identify connections for troubleshooting
quiz.explanation: Labels help anyone service the system safely and quickly.

quiz.q: What is the recommended tilt angle for solar panels in southern Africa?
quiz.explanation: This angle captures optimal sunlight year-round.

quiz.q: What should you do if an inverter beeps continuously?
quiz.explanation: Beeping indicates a fault, often from wiring or overload.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a surge protection device (SPD)?
options: B) To protect against power surges
D) To convert AC to DC
quiz.explanation: SPDs divert excess voltage to ground, protecting equipment.

quiz.q: What is the first step in testing a newly wired system?
options: B) Check all connections are tight
quiz.explanation: Loose connections can cause fires or damage.

quiz.q: What should battery voltage be for a fully charged 24V lead-acid bank?
quiz.explanation: A fully charged 24V bank reads about 25.6V at rest.

quiz.q: What is the maximum allowable voltage drop for battery cables?
quiz.explanation: Keeping voltage drop under 3% ensures efficient power transfer.

quiz.q: What is a hybrid inverter?
options: B) Can use solar, battery, and grid
quiz.explanation: Hybrid inverters manage multiple power sources.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a distribution board in a solar system?
options: A) To house breakers for circuits
C) To convert DC to AC
quiz.explanation: It provides a central point for AC circuit protection.

quiz.q: How often should you test breakers?
quiz.explanation: Monthly testing ensures they will operate when needed.

quiz.q: What is the risk of bypassing a breaker?
quiz.explanation: Bypassing removes overcurrent protection, risking fire.

quiz.q: What tool is essential for checking polarity?
quiz.explanation: A multimeter measures voltage and indicates polarity.

quiz.q: What should you do before working on AC wiring?
quiz.explanation: Turning off inverter prevents electric shock.

quiz.q: What is the recommended cable size for AC loads in a small business?
quiz.explanation: 2.5mmÂ² is standard for 16-20A circuits.

quiz.q: What does a charge controller do?
quiz.explanation: It prevents overcharging and optimizes solar input.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to check if a breaker trips?
quiz.explanation: Resetting without finding fault can cause repeated trips or damage.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of documenting your solar installation?
quiz.explanation: Documentation aids troubleshooting and servicing.

quiz.q: What should you record in a system logbook?
quiz.explanation: All these data help monitor system health.

quiz.q: What is a safe practice when connecting batteries?
quiz.explanation: Insulated tools prevent short circuits and sparks.
